claims.text: The governing distance is the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record convenience copy: EV-GPS-00105 records trace_distance_km of 54.16 km against the booking-time optimal of 36.0 km on EV-TRIP-00105 — an excess of 18.16 km, which is 50.4% of optimal and roughly 23 times the 0.8 km absolute floor. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass, and the same excess breaches the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate, so the deviation is both ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL on this trip's own measurement.

POL-RD-02 recomputation on the booked optimal route: (3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 + 0.28 x 42.0) x 1.0, the surge_multiplier read from EV-FARE-00105 — the only artifact that carries it — plus the 0.80 platform fee, gives a recomputed_fare of 43.36. Charged_total is 65.13, so the refund is 65.13 minus 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to 21.80. That is 33.4% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so standing alone POL-RD-02 would yield a PARTIAL_REFUND of 21.80.

The deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own evidence — the unbroken 427-fix GPS trace plus the chat log — so POL-RD-06 is engaged, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 4 meets the clause's threshold of 3: the repeat-deviation pattern is established. I disclose that EV-DPROF-00105 is IMPAIRED, issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT, weight_multiplier 0.75, and state that the 4-against-3 finding survives that discount. Under POL-RD-06(b) the remedy is FULL_REFUND of charged_total (65.13) rather than the POL-RD-02 figure of 21.80, and the ruling must print both figures side by side so the uplift is auditable.

The same established pattern additionally requires a REFERRAL to driver-conduct review under POL-RD-06(c). That referral is an addition to the monetary ruling, not an escalation, and does not displace or delay it. (EV-DPROF-00105 is the impaired artifact disclosed above — STALE_SNAPSHOT, weight_multiplier 0.75.)

The driver's only explanation is that traffic was heavy on the PIE. No LTA advisory covering the 14:26-15:44 trip window is on file: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0. Under POL-RD-13 an external-traffic excuse is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else; that comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and under POL-RD-08 the assertion carries no weight. Because the driver names no advisory identifier at all, this is a gap in the bundle rather than a conflict in it, so the absence does not escalate under POL-RD-10(5). The deviation therefore stands at the measured 18.16 km and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked 36.0 km optimal.

No other exculpatory clause can run on this record. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00105) contains only two rider queries and a non-answer from the driver — there is no rider instruction to detour, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable, and the route actually driven via town, the East Coast and Bedok is nowhere near the PIE corridor the driver invokes. Neither pickup_amended_at nor dropoff_amended_at is set on EV-TRIP-00105, so POL-RD-05 cannot run; the vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 cannot run. Nothing reduces the excess before materiality is assessed.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: EV-GPS-00105 carries 427 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, zero gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires, so no independent-corroboration requirement arises and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged — the case is decided on the trace as measured.

On burden under POL-RD-08: EV-TRIP-00105, EV-GPS-00105 and EV-FARE-00105 all carry trip_id TRP-00105 with consistent timestamps, which satisfies limb (a), and the excess is measured from an unimpaired trace, which satisfies limb (b). The burden shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; he points to none, and a bare assertion that traffic was bad does not discharge it. The rider-side corroboration trigger does not apply here because rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0.

The chat log independently corroborates the rider's account of the route: at 14:58 he asks why they are heading toward the city, and at 15:19 he reports passing Bedok — both timestamps sit inside the trace window and describe a route that left the optimal PIE corridor. That is an undisputed record, from the disputed trip itself, that the driver took the long way rather than any recognised alternative.

The fare carries no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines — all 0.0 on EV-FARE-00105 — which is correct, since the Changi surcharge is levied only on trips ORIGINATING at the airport and this trip terminates there. There is therefore no pass-through line to add to or subtract from the distance-and-time refund, no double-count risk under POL-RD-09(1), and no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) for either side to raise.

claims.text: The driver does not contest that a deviation is established, so the tribunal should spend its time on remedy. The trace EV-GPS-00105 is unbroken — 427 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 s — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and, per POL-RD-01, its figure governs over the rounded trip-record copy: 54.16 km against the 36.0 km booked optimal is an excess of 18.16 km, or 50.44%, which clears both establishment gates and both materiality gates. That being so, the only remedies in play are the arithmetic refund of POL-RD-02 and, if the Judge is satisfied on the profile, the uplift in POL-RD-06(b) — not the whole-fare refund the rider demands.

The driver's account on the file — that PIE traffic was heavy so he took another way — cannot be weighed, and the driver does not ask the tribunal to weigh it. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00105-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT): no advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, and none carries a validity window overlapping the 14:26-15:44 trip. POL-RD-03 is therefore unavailable on this record and, under POL-RD-13, the assertion is tested against the trip's traffic advisory and nothing else. The driver pointed to no advisory ID, so under POL-RD-08 the assertion cites no evidence and carries no weight: the excess stands at the measured figure and no closure-adjusted optimal arises.

The full-fare uplift under POL-RD-06(b) should not be applied here, and I disclose the impairment on which that submission rests. The pattern is carried by a single artifact, EV-DPROF-00105, which is IMPAIRED: issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT, weight 0.75, the snapshot dated 2026-07-11 08:00 being 108 hours before filing against a 72-hour currency threshold and four days BEFORE this trip. The pattern passes only on the absolute limb — deviation_flags_90d of 4 against a threshold of 3 — while the ratio limb is 4/344 = 0.012 against a threshold of 0.05, and the lifetime near-synonym prior_deviation_flags (6) may not be substituted for the 90-day counter that POL-RD-06 names (POL-GEN-01 forbids the substitution). Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence in a fact carried solely by that artifact is capped at 0.75, and under POL-GEN-02(3) the Judge must name the artifact, its weight and its issue codes; a 43.33 SGD uplift (65.13 charged against the 21.80 POL-RD-02 refund) should not be built on a stale, pre-trip, down-weighted snapshot. The driver's rating, acceptance rate, lifetime trips, cancellation rate and active region are context only under POL-GEN-01 and cannot carry any finding.

Declining the uplift, the remedy is fixed arithmetic and the rider's demand for the whole fare is not a licensed one. Recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 36.0 km + 0.28 x 42.0 min) x 1.0 surge, + 0.80 platform fee = 43.36; the refund is 65.13 - 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to 21.80, which is 33.4% of the charged total and far short of the 90% that would convert a partial refund into a full one. The rider asks for the entire fare and expressly 'not a partial adjustment', but POL-RD-02 makes the refund arithmetic rather than discretionary, and POL-GEN-03 returns the whole contested amount only where the filing party is entirely right.

Nothing may be added on top of that figure. The fare carries no ERP or toll lines at all — erp_gantries is empty and tolls_erp is 0.00 — and no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.00, correctly so, because a Changi surcharge attaches only to trips ORIGINATING at the airport and this trip terminates there). POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule therefore leaves no off-route pass-through to itemise, and POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom gantry or surcharge line to refund. The surge multiplier was read from the fare_breakdown (1.0), not from the trip record, and surge_amount is 0.00, so no surge uplift inflates the recomputation.

The contested sum is the published rate card applied to the distance and time actually driven, not a penalty or a discretionary charge that could be stripped out beyond the recomputation: 3.80 base + 40.65 distance (54.2 km at 0.75) + 19.88 time (71 min at 0.28) + 0.80 platform fee = 65.13, with no surge, toll, waiting or premium line anywhere in the breakdown. There is accordingly no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) and nothing in this fare that the driver should be made to give back beyond the POL-RD-02 arithmetic.

The rider's narrative of nearly missing check-in does not enlarge the remedy. The rider's own message in the chat log puts the flight at 17:15, and the trip record shows the vehicle reaching the dropoff at 15:44:05; no artifact on the file records a missed or nearly missed check-in, and the driver's own statement on the record is that the passenger reached the airport in time. Inconvenience is not a head of relief in this vocabulary — POL-RD-02 gives arithmetic and POL-GEN-03 gives the whole contested amount only where the claim is fully made out — so the timing narrative supports neither the whole-fare demand nor any sum beyond the recomputation.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the driver took a materially longer route and I am refunding the whole SGD 65.13 that was charged.

ROUTE. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00105 is complete — 427 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 s — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and its figure governs over the rounded trip-record copy (POL-RD-01). It records 54.16 km driven against the 36.0 km booked optimal on EV-TRIP-00105: an excess of 18.16 km, or 50.44%. That clears both establishment gates and both materiality gates of POL-RD-01, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL. The rider's measurement claim is accepted and the driver does not contest it.

EXCULPATION. None runs. The driver's statement that PIE traffic was heavy is unsupported by any traffic advisory. The bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00105-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT). The driver names no advisory ID, so under POL-RD-13(1) the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it and does not escalate under POL-RD-10(5); under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13(2) the uncited assertion carries no weight and the excess stands at the measured figure. POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record. POL-RD-04 finds no rider instruction to detour in the chat log (EV-CHAT-00105); POL-RD-05 finds no amended pickup or dropoff; POL-RD-12 does not apply (vehicle_type RYDE_X, not pooled).

THE POL-RD-02 FIGURE. (Base fare 3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 km + 0.28 x 42.0 min) x surge 1.0, read from EV-FARE-00105, the only artifact carrying the multiplier + platform fee 0.80 = recomputed_fare 43.36. Charged_total on EV-FARE-00105 is 65.13. Refund = 65.13 - 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to 21.80 — 33.4% of the charge, below the 90% full-refund share. The driver's claim that the remedy is fixed at this figure is accepted as the POL-RD-02 figure and rejected as the final remedy, for the reason below.

THE POL-RD-06 UPLIFT. A MATERIAL deviation requires the driver-profile check, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d on EV-DPROF-00105 is 4, at or above the clause's threshold of 3; the repeat pattern is ESTABLISHED. The test is disjunctive, so the driver's point that the ratio limb (4/344 = 0.012) falls short does not help him, and prior_deviation_flags (6) is a lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting for the 90-day figure. EV-DPROF-00105 is impaired — issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT, weight_multiplier 0.75, its snapshot dated 108 hours before filing against a 72-hour currency threshold and four days before this trip — and I name that impairment here as POL-GEN-02(3) requires; the 4-against-3 finding survives the discount. Because the deviation is also MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own trace, POL-RD-06(b) replaces the POL-RD-02 partial with FULL_REFUND of charged_total. Side by side, as the clause requires: POL-RD-02 partial 21.80; POL-RD-06(b) uplifted figure 65.13. There is no government-set or third-party pass-through line to carve out — EV-FARE-00105 shows no ERP, no tolls and no airport surcharge (the Changi surcharge attaches only to trips ORIGINATING at an airport and this trip terminates there) — so the whole 65.13 is refunded.

POL-RD-09. No ERP or toll lines and no surcharge line, so there is nothing to itemise, no double-count risk under limb (1), and no billing-integrity defect under limb (4) for either side.

THE RIDER'S NARRATIVE. The rider is refunded the whole fare, but not because check-in was nearly missed: inconvenience is not a head of relief in this vocabulary and no artifact records a missed or nearly missed check-in, so that part of the claim adds nothing to the remedy.

CONFIDENCE AND ESCALATION. My confidence is capped at 0.75 under POL-GEN-02(2), the weight of EV-DPROF-00105, the only artifact carrying the repeat-pattern fact the uplift rests on. That is at or above the 0.70 confidence floor read from the loaded policy, so the case is decided rather than escalated; I have run each POL-RD-10 trigger and none fires. This ruling differs from precedents P-0001 and P-0002, which share POL-RD-01, POL-RD-02 and POL-RD-08 but carried no POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern finding: it is that finding on EV-DPROF-00105 that lifts this case from a partial to a full refund.

EXECUTION. The monetary effect, 65.13, exceeds the POL-GEN-05 threshold of 8.00, so this provisional ruling issues but the amount is held for release by a human reviewer. Either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.
referrals: POL-RD-06(c): refer the case to driver-conduct review — a repeat deviation pattern (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 4 on EV-DPROF-00105) is established alongside a material, substantiated deviation on this trip (EV-GPS-00105). The referral rides with the refund and does not displace or delay it.

POL-RD-06(b) therefore gives FULL_REFUND of charged_total: 65.13, against the POL-RD-02 figure of 21.80, an uplift of 43.33, printed here so its size is auditable. ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: on the facts of the trip itself you are not really in dispute. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00105 is unbroken — 427 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps, max gap 0.0 s — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), no independent-corroboration requirement arises, and under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs over the rounded trip-record copy. It records 54.16 km against the booking-time optimal of 36.0 km on EV-TRIP-00105: an excess of 18.16 km, or 50.4% of optimal. Both establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and both materiality gates (over 50% and over 8.0 km) pass, so the deviation is established and material on this trip's own measurement.

The driver's explanation — heavy PIE traffic so he took another way — cannot be weighed. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00105-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, so POL-RD-03 cannot run. Because the driver names no advisory identifier, the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a cited artifact contradicted, and it does not escalate the case under POL-RD-10(5) (POL-RD-13(1)). Under POL-RD-08 the assertion cites no evidence and carries no weight: no closure-adjusted optimal arises and the excess stands at 18.16 km. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires — identifiers and timestamps across EV-TRIP-00105, EV-GPS-00105 and EV-FARE-00105 match, and no charge line is unmatched.

The arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run against the booked optimal route: (3.80 base + 0.75 × 36.0 km + 0.28 × 42.0 min) × 1.0 surge — the multiplier read from EV-FARE-00105, the only artifact that carries it — + 0.80 platform fee = 43.36. Charged_total is 65.13, so the POL-RD-02 refund is 21.77, rounded up to 21.80. That is 33.4% of the charge, short of the 90% that would make a full refund on the arithmetic alone.

POL-RD-06 is engaged because the deviation is material. EV-DPROF-00105 records deviation_flags_90d = 4 against the clause's threshold of 3, so the repeat-deviation pattern is established; the ratio limb (4/344) is not required because the clause is disjunctive, and prior_deviation_flags (6) is a lifetime near-synonym that POL-GEN-01 forbids putting in place of the trailing-90-day counter. I name the impairment as POL-GEN-02(3) requires: this artifact is down-weighted to 0.75 with issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT (snapshot 2026-07-11 08:00, 108 hours before filing against a 72-hour threshold). The 4-against-3 finding survives that discount. Under POL-RD-06(b) a material, substantiated deviation licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total, so the two figures are printed side by side: the POL-RD-02 figure is 21.80 and the uplifted figure is 65.13. There are no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines to settle separately — all 0.00 on EV-FARE-00105, correctly so, since the Changi surcharge attaches only to trips originating at the airport and this trip terminates there — so nothing is carved out of the uplift and no POL-RD-09(1) double-count arises. There is no phantom line and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding.

Under POL-RD-06(c) the case is additionally referred to driver-conduct review. That referral rides with the money and does not displace or delay it.

Both requests are answered. The rider asked for the entire fare and gets it, but on the POL-RD-06(b) uplift, not because the trip ran long against a flight time: the rider's timing narrative adds no separate head of relief and the driver was not shown to have missed anything that the record supports. The driver asked for the arithmetic-only figure and is not given it, for the reason above. The driver's rating, acceptance rate, lifetime trips, cancellation rate and active region are context only under POL-GEN-01 and carry no weight here.

Confidence is 0.75, capped under POL-GEN-02(2) by EV-DPROF-00105, the sole artifact carrying the pattern fact; that is above the 0.70 escalation floor. The monetary effect of 65.13 exceeds the automatic-execution threshold, so the amount is issued but held for release by a human reviewer under POL-GEN-05, and either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

The burden shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; he points to none, and a bare assertion that traffic was bad does not discharge it. The chat log independently corroborates the rider's account of the route: at 14:58 he asks why they are heading toward the city, and at 15:19 he reports passing Bedok — both timestamps sit inside the trace window and describe a route that left the optimal PIE corridor. That is an undisputed record, from the disputed trip itself, that the driver took the long way rather than any recognised alternative.

The fare carries no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines — all 0.0 on EV-FARE-00105 — which is correct, since the Changi surcharge is levied only on trips ORIGINATING at the airport and this trip terminates there. There is therefore no pass-through line to add to or subtract from the distance-and-time refund, no double-count risk under POL-RD-09(1), and no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) for either side to raise.

The driver does not contest that a deviation is established, so the tribunal should spend its time on remedy. The trace EV-GPS-00105 is unbroken — 427 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 s — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and, per POL-RD-01, its figure governs over the rounded trip-record copy: 54.16 km against the 36.0 km booked optimal is an excess of 18.16 km, or 50.44%, which clears both establishment gates and both materiality gates. That being so, the only remedies in play are the arithmetic refund of POL-RD-02 and, if the Judge is satisfied on the profile, the uplift in POL-RD-06(b) — not the whole-fare refund the rider demands.

The driver's account on the file — that PIE traffic was heavy so he took another way — cannot be weighed, and the driver does not ask the tribunal to weigh it. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00105-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT): no advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, and none carries a validity window overlapping the 14:26-15:44 trip. POL-RD-03 is therefore unavailable on this record and, under POL-RD-13, the assertion is tested against the trip's traffic advisory and nothing else. The driver pointed to no advisory ID, so under POL-RD-08 the assertion cites no evidence and carries no weight: the excess stands at the measured figure and no closure-adjusted optimal arises.

The full-fare uplift under POL-RD-06(b) should not be applied here, and I disclose the impairment on which that submission rests. The pattern is carried by a single artifact, EV-DPROF-00105, which is IMPAIRED: issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT, weight 0.75, the snapshot dated 2026-07-11 08:00 being 108 hours before filing against a 72-hour currency threshold and four days BEFORE this trip. The pattern passes only on the absolute limb — deviation_flags_90d of 4 against a threshold of 3 — while the ratio limb is 4/344 = 0.012 against a threshold of 0.05, and the lifetime near-synonym prior_deviation_flags (6) may not be substituted for the 90-day counter that POL-RD-06 names (POL-GEN-01 forbids the substitution). Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence in a fact carried solely by that artifact is capped at 0.75, and under POL-GEN-02(3) the Judge must name the artifact, its weight and its issue codes; a 43.33 SGD uplift (65.13 charged against the 21.80 POL-RD-02 refund) should not be built on a stale, pre-trip, down-weighted snapshot. The driver's rating, acceptance rate, lifetime trips, cancellation rate and active region are context only under POL-GEN-01 and cannot carry any finding.

ledger.claim: Declining the uplift, the remedy is fixed arithmetic and the rider's demand for the whole fare is not a licensed one. Recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 36.0 km + 0.28 x 42.0 min) x 1.0 surge, + 0.80 platform fee = 43.36; the refund is 65.13 - 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to 21.80, which is 33.4% of the charged total and far short of the 90% that would convert a partial refund into a full one. The rider asks for the entire fare and expressly 'not a partial adjustment', but POL-RD-02 makes the refund arithmetic rather than discretionary, and POL-GEN-03 returns the whole contested amount only where the filing party is entirely right.

Nothing may be added on top of that figure. The fare carries no ERP or toll lines at all — erp_gantries is empty and tolls_erp is 0.00 — and no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.00, correctly so, because a Changi surcharge attaches only to trips ORIGINATING at the airport and this trip terminates there). POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule therefore leaves no off-route pass-through to itemise, and POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom gantry or surcharge line to refund. The surge multiplier was read from the fare_breakdown (1.0), not from the trip record, and surge_amount is 0.00, so no surge uplift inflates the recomputation.

The contested sum is the published rate card applied to the distance and time actually driven, not a penalty or a discretionary charge that could be stripped out beyond the recomputation: 3.80 base + 40.65 distance (54.2 km at 0.75) + 19.88 time (71 min at 0.28) + 0.80 platform fee = 65.13, with no surge, toll, waiting or premium line anywhere in the breakdown. There is accordingly no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) and nothing in this fare that the driver should be made to give back beyond the POL-RD-02 arithmetic.

The rider's narrative of nearly missing check-in does not enlarge the remedy. The rider's own message in the chat log puts the flight at 17:15, and the trip record shows the vehicle reaching the dropoff at 15:44:05; no artifact on the file records a missed or nearly missed check-in, and the driver's own statement on the record is that the passenger reached the airport in time. Inconvenience is not a head of relief in this vocabulary — POL-RD-02 gives arithmetic and POL-GEN-03 gives the whole contested amount only where the claim is fully made out — so the timing narrative supports neither the whole-fare demand nor any sum beyond the recomputation.
